pitch_detail.notes: Lower wall in the seasonal water streaks; wet early in the season, best climbed early in the day. Portaledge site at pitch 3.
Upper wall. Portaledge site at pitch 12; the 15th belay is the only one without bolts.

wa_mount_index_north_norwegian_buttress.beta: Jötnar follows a watercourse up the left side of the North Norwegian Buttress. The lower half runs through seasonal water streaks and is wet early in the summer; the seepage pitches go best early in the morning. The aid cruxes are pitch 4 (A3+) and pitch 9 (A3). Every belay is bolted except the 15th, and there are no natural ledges, so a portaledge is required; good portaledge sites are at pitches 3, 6 and 12. Loose blocks were cleaned after the first ascent, but expect loose rock. Most parties approach via Lake Serene.
wa_mount_index_north_norwegian_buttress.overview: Jötnar is a Grade VI big-wall aid route on the North Norwegian Buttress, the roughly 2,000-foot buttress on Mount Index above Lake Serene, separated from the smaller South Norwegian Buttress by a deep cleft between the Main and Middle summits. It follows a continuous crack system on the left side of the buttress, about 100 yards left of the original 1980s Doorish aid line, for 16 pitches at 5.9 A3+. The belays are bolted, and reasonably experienced wall climbers can expect three to four days on the wall with a portaledge; the first ascent took seven.
wa_mount_index_north_norwegian_buttress.descent_text: Jötnar is descended by rappelling the route, not by a walk-off. All of its belays are bolted except the 15th, which is a gear anchor, so back it up or leave gear there. Much of the wall overhangs: on rappel you can end up hanging free of the rock and need a swing or a directional to reach the next station. Strip the wall as you go and retrieve any fixed lines. Haul bags can be lowered a long way down the lower wall, since the overhang leaves little to snag them on. From the base, reverse the talus traverse around Lake Serene to the maintained trail.
wa_mount_index_north_norwegian_buttress.rappels: Rappel the route off its bolted belays (the 15th belay is a gear anchor); overhanging pitches need swings or directionals to reach the next station.
wa_mount_index_north_norwegian_buttress.fa: Sam Boyce, Lani Chapko and Kyle Willis, August 2020
